name: Heterozygous Beta-Thalassemia Intermedia with Supernumerary Alpha-Globin Gene
aliases: Beta-Thalassemia Intermedia with Alpha-Globin Gene Triplication
Heterozygous Beta-Thalassemia with Alpha-Globin Gene Duplication

criteria.description: Presence of heterozygous beta-globin gene mutation confirmed by molecular genetic testing
Detection of alpha-globin gene triplication or quadruplication by genetic analysis
Chronic mild to moderate microcytic hypochromic anemia with hemoglobin levels typically between 7-10 g/dL
Elevated HbA2 and variable HbF levels on hemoglobin electrophoresis
Clinical features consistent with thalassemia intermedia including mild splenomegaly and absence of transfusion dependency

diagnosticCriteria.minimumForDiagnosis: Presence of heterozygous beta-thalassemia mutation plus supernumerary alpha-globin gene with clinical and laboratory evidence of thalassemia intermedia phenotype
diagnosticCriteria.notes: Genetic testing is essential to differentiate from simple beta-thalassemia trait and other hemoglobinopathies.

pathognomonic.symptomName: Mild to moderate microcytic hypochromic anemia
pathognomonic.notes: Characteristic laboratory finding in affected individuals
Mild to moderate enlargement of the spleen

common.symptomName: Elevated HbA2 levels on hemoglobin electrophoresis

common.notes: Resulting from increased red blood cell turnover
searchTerms: slight jaundice from red blood cell breakdown

common.symptomName: Bone marrow expansion with mild facial bone deformities
searchTerms: expanded bone marrow causing mild facial changes
bone marrow growth with slight face bone deformities
mild facial bone shape changes from marrow expansion

occasional.notes: Occur due to chronic anemia and vascular changes
Enlargement of the liver due to extramedullary hematopoiesis

searchTerms: chronic fatigue due to low red blood cells

rare.notes: Due to increased intestinal iron absorption
searchTerms: excess iron in body without blood transfusion
iron overload not caused by transfusions
blood cell production outside bone marrow

laboratory: Microcytic hypochromic anemia with hemoglobin 7-10 g/dL
Elevated HbA2 (>3.5%) and variable HbF on hemoglobin electrophoresis
Normal to mildly elevated reticulocyte count
Increased serum ferritin in absence of transfusions
imaging: Bone marrow expansion visible on skull and long bone X-rays
Splenomegaly and mild hepatomegaly on abdominal ultrasound
Paraspinal masses on MRI in rare cases of extramedullary hematopoiesis
other: Absence of transfusion dependency distinguishes from beta-thalassemia major
Mild to moderate clinical phenotype with variable severity

distinguishingFeatures: Normal or mildly elevated HbA2 without clinical intermedia phenotype
Homozygous or compound heterozygous beta-globin mutations
Marked bone deformities and growth retardation
Variable clinical severity depending on gene dosage

redFlags: Signs of iron overload despite no transfusions
